questions.title: Legal settlement
questions.scenario: The company is defending a lawsuit. On May 10, based on developments and outside counsel's advice, management concludes an unfavorable outcome is probable and estimates the loss at $12–18 million. The parties do not agree in principle to $14 million until May 20.
questions.question: When is the loss contingency first recognized?
answers: When the plaintiff first offers to settle
May 10 — loss becomes probable and reasonably estimable
questions.explanation: Recognition is driven by the loss becoming probable and reasonably estimable. Agreement, signature and payment are later events.

questions.title: Building fire
questions.scenario: A fire severely damages an insured distribution center on January 15. Management estimates the damage on January 18; the insurer confirms coverage later.
questions.question: What triggers recognition of the property loss?
questions.explanation: The casualty event causes the asset loss. Insurance recovery is a separate accounting analysis.

questions.title: Demand collapse
questions.scenario: A product's sales slow 10%, then a competitor launches a better product. In Q3 market prices for the company's product fall 40%. The product is discontinued in Q4.
questions.question: Which event most clearly triggers reassessment of inventory carrying value?
questions.explanation: The significant market-price decline is direct evidence that inventory valuation needs reassessment.

questions.title: Loss of a major customer
questions.scenario: A customer represents 28% of revenue of a reporting unit with significant goodwill. New facts cause management to conclude the likely customer loss may materially reduce the reporting unit's fair value.
questions.question: When should the company perform an interim goodwill impairment triggering-event assessment?
answers: When facts indicate the likely loss may materially affect reporting-unit fair value
questions.explanation: The trigger is the change in facts indicating it may be more likely than not that reporting-unit fair value is below carrying amount. Assessment does not automatically mean impairment.

questions.title: Established severance plan
questions.scenario: The company has a long-standing severance plan known and understood by employees. On January 20 the authorized decision-maker commits to terminate identified employees and the applicable recognition criteria are met. Employees are informed January 25.
questions.question: When is the severance obligation recognized?
questions.explanation: For this established severance arrangement, the recognition point is the authorized termination decision/commitment when the applicable criteria are satisfied.

questions.title: Exit from a leased building
questions.scenario: The company decides to exit a leased office while continuing to occupy it and negotiating with the landlord.
questions.question: Which events can trigger relevant lease accounting consequences? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: An agreed amendment can trigger modification accounting, while complete cessation of use can trigger other relevant accounting consequences.

questions.title: Adverse court judgment
questions.scenario: The company previously concluded loss in a material lawsuit was not probable. A court then issues an adverse $25 million judgment; the company intends to appeal.
questions.question: What most clearly requires immediate reassessment?
questions.explanation: The adverse judgment is significant new evidence requiring immediate reassessment. An appeal does not make it irrelevant.

questions.title: Customer bankruptcy after year-end
questions.scenario: A major customer owes $9 million at December 31 and is already paying slowly. It files for bankruptcy January 25, before the financial statements are issued.
questions.question: What provides the strongest subsequent evidence about a condition that may have existed at year-end?
questions.explanation: A bankruptcy shortly after year-end may provide additional evidence about financial distress existing at the balance-sheet date.

questions.title: Fire after year-end
questions.scenario: A building is undamaged at December 31. On January 15, before financial statements are issued, a fire destroys it.
questions.question: Should the fire loss be recognized at December 31?
answers: No — it arose after year-end; consider disclosure
No — subsequent events are never disclosed
questions.explanation: The fire reflects a condition arising after year-end, so it is generally nonrecognized, although material disclosure may be needed.

questions.title: Litigation range
questions.scenario: A litigation loss is probable. The reasonable estimate is $12–18 million and no amount is a better estimate than another.
questions.question: How much should be accrued under US GAAP?
questions.explanation: US GAAP generally accrues the low end when no amount within a reasonably estimated range is a better estimate.

questions.title: Reasonably possible lawsuit
questions.scenario: A material $20 million litigation loss is reasonably possible, but not probable.
questions.question: What is the appropriate response?
questions.explanation: A reasonably possible but not probable loss is generally not accrued, but applicable disclosure requirements should be evaluated.

questions.title: Insurance recovery
questions.scenario: The company recognizes an $8 million casualty loss and expects its insurer to reimburse $7 million.
questions.question: How should the expected recovery affect the casualty loss?
answers: Recognize the casualty loss and analyze recovery separately
Record the full recovery regardless of uncertainty
questions.explanation: The casualty loss and insurance recovery are separate accounting matters.

questions.title: The 60-hour solution
questions.scenario: Your accounting team has worked 60-hour weeks for three months because of persistent hiring challenges.
questions.question: How should management improve morale?
answers: Pizza party — one topping per employee
Free soda voucher for Sandy's — no refills
questions.explanation: Pizza has repeatedly demonstrated the ability to address structural capacity issues without changing headcount.

questions.title: Engagement crisis
questions.scenario: Finance engagement scores have fallen 23 points.
questions.question: What should leadership do?
answers: Repeat the survey daily until results are satisfactory
questions.explanation: The underlying problem has not changed, but the sample size is now excellent.

questions.title: The PBC loop
questions.scenario: The auditors request a reconciliation that was on Tab 3 of yesterday's workbook.
questions.question: What should you do?
answers: Rename it FINAL_v4_UPDATED.xlsx and send it again
questions.explanation: The auditors thank you for the additional information.

questions.title: Close status
questions.scenario: The CFO asks whether close is on schedule. It is two days behind.
questions.question: What is the appropriate response?
answers: We continue to make good progress against an ambitious timeline
questions.explanation: Excellent executive presence. The calendar remains unchanged, but confidence has improved materially.

questions.title: Urgent CEO request
questions.scenario: An email apparently from the CEO asks you to buy $2,000 of gift cards and text the codes.
questions.question: What should you do?
answers: Forward to all Finance asking if anyone knows whether it's real
Report it using the phishing process
questions.explanation: Congratulations. You have increased organizational awareness by approximately 400 recipients.

questions.title: Workplace stress
questions.scenario: Finance leadership wants to reduce employee stress without reducing workload.
questions.question: Which initiative best demonstrates commitment to wellness?
questions.explanation: Attendance will be tracked. Please bring your own lunch.

questions.title: Digital transformation
questions.scenario: Finance's general ledger is slow, cumbersome and increasingly unsupported.
questions.question: What is the appropriate modernization strategy?
answers: Unlock the previous version of Oracle GL
questions.explanation: Several features from 2014 have now been restored. Transformation complete.

questions.title: High performer
questions.scenario: Your employee is performing extremely well and requires little supervision.
questions.question: How should you recognize their independence?
answers: Increase quarterly check-ins to weekly for the next year
questions.explanation: We don't want success to interfere with development.
